capture.final_message:
View fractional ideals as \(R\)-submodules of the localization \(P\). Prove the four universally quantified statements independently, then form the two biconditionals.

The useful intermediate facts are:

- the fractional ideal \(1\), coerced to a submodule of \(P\), is the scalar-generated submodule \(1\);
- the ordinary ideal \(\bot\), embedded as a fractional ideal, becomes \(0\);
- \(1\in (1:\operatorname{FractionalIdeal} R\,S\,P)\);
- when \(K\) is a fraction ring of \(R\) at the non-zero-divisors, the map
  \[
  I\longmapsto \operatorname{coeIdeal}(I)
  \]
  is an order embedding, hence
  \[
  \operatorname{coeIdeal}(I)\le \operatorname{coeIdeal}(J)
  \iff I\le J.
  \]

These are essentially normalization/coercion lemmas; alternatively, each can be shown by extensionality and unfolding membership in the localized submodule. The essential assumption in the last item is `IsFractionRing`: it supplies the faithful localization representation needed to reflect, rather than merely preserve, ideal inclusion. Once all four facts are established, both `Iff`s and the outer `And` follow propositionally.
